markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize **uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy on corrected NextItNet**, before adding gates or mining. This is a training-objective experiment; no improvement is claimed.

Three starting-point insights guide selection. First, the supplied baseline inspiration scores 0.5300 versus 0.5163–0.5175 for gate proposals; without matched-run evidence, these differences justify caution, not architectural conclusions. Second, Electronics has 6.84% sampled training wrong ranks and a 0.4512 tenth-percentile margin, motivating stronger discrimination. Third, terminal-preserving permutations worsen training-target ranks, demonstrating earlier-history dependence; sparse replacement support prevents diagnosing excessive recency dependence.

Related work supplies three complementary insights. [NextItNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163) supports sampled-softmax training, making objective experiments family-compatible. [Wu et al.](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf) motivate competitive-negative weighting, but uncorrected candidate CE differs from corrected sampled softmax. [Hard-negative theory](https://doi.org/10.1145/3543507.3583223) and [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) motivate controlled hardness and caution about false negatives; neither establishes this proposal’s effectiveness.

The conceptual framework separates **candidate discrimination** (objective), **historical evidence selection** (causal gates), and **candidate exposure** (sampling). Test these separately to preserve attribution.

Scores use originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Positive and negative reasons address each score in that order.

| Atomic idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform multi-negative cross-entropy | 3/6/5/8/4 | Diagnosis-specific comparison; useful control; targets competing associations; addresses weak separation; unchanged inference | Established objective; uncertain transfer; indirect recency targeting; margins are in-sample; sampling and memory require care |
| Recent-summary residual gate | 4/6/8/6/4 | Contextual adaptation; extensible; directly conditions recent evidence; may improve discrimination; localized projection | Established gating; static scaling possible; shortcuts retain history; bottleneck unproven; predictor synchronization required |
| Moderate-hard negative curriculum | 4/6/6/7/5 | Controlled curriculum; extensible sampling; challenges plausible distractors; targets competitive errors; uses existing scorer | Established mining; uncertain transfer; false negatives; training bias; additional scoring and reproducibility work |

**Selected experiment.** Keep the ungated corrected backbone; compare candidate CE against multi-negative BCE using identical sets of 32 distinct uniform negatives. CE uses one shared denominator; BCE uses positive loss plus mean negative loss. Matching candidates does not match gradient scale: record gradient norms and exact reductions.

Explicit behavioral hypotheses are fewer broadly associated candidates displacing specific matches and fewer isolated older-interest associations displacing current matches. Both require qualitative verification; CE introduces no recency mechanism and cannot establish compatibility or unmet need. Electronics’ weak sampled separation is the model-facing target.

Logical steps: sample eligible negatives → score candidates → apply CE → update one network. Chunk complete sequence examples with immediate backward and one optimizer step; retain all 33 candidates together. Preserve four routes, seeds, limits and host selection. Track margins and prescribed qualitative outcomes alongside sampled-candidate macro HR@10. [Sampled metrics](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) do not establish full-catalog gains. Use descriptive paired uncertainty when available, disclose validation search, and defer gates/mining. Load one selected checkpoint per category.

idea.description: Test uniform multi-negative candidate cross-entropy on the supplied corrected, ungated NextItNet, using a matched multi-negative BCE comparison. Preserve one independently trained network and one selected checkpoint per category. Treat this as an objective ablation with indirect behavioral hypotheses, rather than a demonstrated solution to recency or compatibility failures.
idea.motivation: Electronics has a measured 6.84% sampled training negative-beats-positive rate and a 0.4512 tenth-percentile margin, substantially weaker separation than the other categories. Candidate competition offers a practical hypothesis for reducing two user-observed failures: broadly associated recommendations displacing specific current matches, and recommendations linked to isolated older interests displacing current matches. These are explicit behavioral targets, not established effects: the objective supplies neither a recency mechanism nor evidence about compatibility, duplicate function, replacement or replenishment needs. The supplied gate inspirations have lower reported scores than the baseline inspiration, supporting a cautious objective-first experiment without establishing why those differences occurred or whether they exceed evaluation variability. At 20% research progress, retain the gate and moderate-hard curriculum as subsequent alternatives rather than introducing additional mechanisms before measuring this comparison.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain the corrected baseline's causal dilated-convolution backbone, item embeddings, scoring head, optimizer, initialization, family-specific sample_batch, splits and routing. Do not carry forward an experimental gate as the cold start. Record inherited settings rather than inventing missing baseline details. Keep the same architecture and inference computation in both objective conditions.

For each valid aligned next-item training position, draw K=32 distinct uniform negative item IDs. Exclude padding, the target and that user's complete known training-history positives; never consult validation or test labels for exclusion. This complete-history exclusion policy uses public training interactions, including items later than the sampled prefix, and therefore changes the training objective relative to prefix-only or target-only exclusion. Apply it identically across losses and disclose it. It removes known collisions, not latent false negatives. User IDs needed for exclusion must remain available internally in the sampler; do not change the public diagnostic loader contract to expose them.

Use uniform rejection sampling with a per-position set, accepting only eligible IDs not already accepted. For a small eligible pool, enumerate its IDs and sample without replacement instead. Both methods must sample the same uniform-without-replacement distribution; do not use a retry cap followed by a biased fallback. If the eligible pool contains M<K items, use all M with an explicit candidate mask. A position with M=0 contributes no candidate loss and must be counted in diagnostics. Normalize loss over eligible valid positions, rather than counting skipped positions as zero losses. If the entire batch has no eligible positions, skip the optimizer step and record it. Never include padded IDs in either loss.

Compute unnormalized baseline logits, with the positive in candidate column zero. Use temperature 1 and candidate cross-entropy L_CE = -s_pos + logsumexp(s_pos, s_neg1, ..., s_negK). This is an uncorrected candidate-ranking objective, not an unbiased estimate of full-catalog likelihood or an implementation of corrected sampled softmax. Eligible sampling pools vary by user. With uniform sampling without replacement, a negative's inclusion probability is min(K,M)/M, whereas the positive is always included; a common logit correction does not automatically cancel. Do not add an expected-count correction in this experiment. Any corrected sampled-softmax comparison would require a separately specified sampler-consistent objective. Do not add cosine normalization, an auxiliary fitted scorer, text features, gates or mining.

If budget permits the matched comparison, use L_BCE = softplus(-s_pos) + mean_j softplus(s_neg_j) per eligible valid position. This gives equal aggregate positive and negative group weights. It differs from both averaging all K+1 BCE terms and summing all negative terms. Match candidate sets, eligible positions, batch ordering and shared initialization across the two losses. Matching K does not match relative example weighting or gradient magnitude. Retain the inherited optimizer and learning rate for the primary controlled comparison; log unclipped gradient-norm summaries and any inherited clipping rate. A separate learning-rate adjustment would be another disclosed search decision rather than a silent fairness correction.

Use a dedicated seed-42 negative-sampling stream independent of model/dropout RNG. Match candidates across objective conditions using a deterministic draw order or stable seed mapping from category, epoch, batch and training-position identity; do not use Python's process-randomized hash. Preserve the inherited sample_batch stream and record sampler version, exclusion policy, candidate count and batch configuration. Report the inherited baseline separately if its objective, negative count or exclusion policy differs. Controls are separate experimental trials whose predictions are never combined. Count every attempted training run and diagnostic against the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance; do not promise a trial count without runtime evidence.

Memory handling must bound both embedding/logit tensors and saved backbone activations. Prefer chunks of complete sequence examples along the batch axis, preserving each sequence's full causal context and scoring all positive-plus-negative candidates together at every supervised position. First determine the full logical batch's eligible-position count N, call zero_grad once, then for each example chunk recompute its backbone forward, sum its eligible losses, divide by N, and call backward immediately. Call the inherited clipping operation, if any, and optimizer step once after all chunks. Do not collect graph-connected losses for a final backward, use retain_graph=True, split a sequence into context-free position chunks, or average separate chunk means. Those approaches respectively retain activations, preserve graphs unnecessarily, change causal context, or change position weighting.

Choose and record a fixed example-chunk size before paired training, using the same partition in both objective conditions. Example chunking preserves the logical position-mean objective, but exact stochastic equivalence to an unchunked run requires matching dropout masks and no batch-dependent state updates. Verify the supplied normalization is compatible; do not silently modify the backbone to accommodate chunking. If direct example chunking is insufficient, gradient caching is a separate implementation option: obtain detached representation gradients, recompute backbone chunks with replayed dropout RNG, and accumulate both backbone and tied item-embedding scoring gradients before one update. Prefer the simpler direct approach for K=32. Candidate-axis chunks require a global shared log-sum-exp and recomputation; summing independent candidate-chunk cross-entropies changes the objective. Do not introduce GradCache or Cut Cross-Entropy dependencies merely because they appear in the references.

Before long training, check CE and BCE formulas, candidate uniqueness/exclusions, valid-position normalization and chunked gradients against a tiny deterministic unchunked batch with dropout disabled, including variable eligible counts and tied item embeddings. Check causal behavior by perturbing future inputs, padding behavior and generated-predictor score agreement. These checks consume the host-accounted budget when executed; no checks have been executed in this report.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution and the supplied validation/checkpoint schedule. Respect the SASREC_EPOCHS environment default of 200 despite its family-agnostic variable name. Example chunks are components of one logical batch, not extra training batches. Select using only pinned host macro validation HR@10 across Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl: arithmetic mean of the four category HR@10 values, each measured on 200 validation users with 99 unique negatives at evaluation seed 42. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'] and trial-local artifacts. Do not inspect other trials, reuse their checkpoints, access hidden test files, fetch extra data or pretrained weights, or modify the evaluator.

Inference architecture remains the corrected baseline. Preserve the predictor writer and verify that its saved configuration, state loading, padding behavior and scores match the trained network. Gather the maximum nonpadding positional index for left-padded histories, never count-1; retain the supplied empty-history convention. Each category loads exactly one selected independently trained model/checkpoint. Preserve all four category routes. Store the objective, sampling configuration and inherited architecture configuration with the checkpoint for auditability; training-only negative sampling introduces no additional prediction component.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items) and host ModelView interfaces. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors B x L; additional training negatives need not change this interface. Preserve the original fixed diagnostic negative protocol for cross-trial comparability. Return measured metrics and explicit metric_definitions. Retain sampled margins, wrong-rank rates and score norms; distinguish candidate-training loss from fixed-protocol diagnostic separation. Treat embedding cosine as alignment rather than proof of collapse. Sparse replacement support cannot establish excessive historical influence, and training-prefix catalog HR@10 is not held-out validation.

Use only the prescribed twenty real training users, five per category, for qualitative follow-up with full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Separately track specific current matches, broad-association displacement, older-interest displacement, duplicate-function or unsupported-compatibility rejection, and uncertain item identity. The selected idea explicitly targets the first two displacement failures as hypotheses; user-alignment remains modest because its mechanism does not directly select recent evidence. Do not infer improved behavior from larger training margins alone. Only public histories, timestamps, item titles and descriptions are available; ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores and simulator traits must remain unavailable. Textual similarity cannot establish physical compatibility or unmet need.

Report host results explicitly as sampled-candidate HR@10. Fixed evaluation candidates support paired comparisons but do not establish full-catalog performance, and sampled metrics can change model orderings. When the host exposes per-user hit indicators, report category differences, gained/lost hits and a category-stratified paired bootstrap: resample users within each category with identical indices for both models, compute each category difference, then average the four differences equally. A reproducible descriptive analysis can use 10,000 replicates, analysis seed 42 and percentile 2.5/97.5 bounds without altering the evaluator. If identities reveal dependent users across routes, use user-level cluster resampling that preserves equal category weighting; otherwise disclose the independence assumption. If host outputs lack paired indicators, state that paired uncertainty is unavailable.

One changed hit changes category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 percentage points. Bootstrap intervals describe hypothetical user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the fitted models and observed candidate sets; the fixed benchmark score itself is deterministic. They exclude training-seed and candidate-redraw variation. Repeated checkpoint/configuration selection on the same validation set creates selection optimism, and bootstrapping the winner does not correct it. Disclose all attempted configurations and retain the inherited checkpoint schedule; reserve confirmatory claims for the host's untouched final evaluation after selection. Popularity, item-frequency and memorization shortcuts remain possible even with uniform negatives; inspect available training-frequency strata descriptively without adding an independently fitted scorer. No execution or validation gain is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
# Apply inside the host-supplied corrected NextItNet training scaffold.
# CE and optional BCE are separate trials; never combine their predictions.
for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    model = corrected_ungated_nextitnet(inherited_config)
    negative_rng = dedicated_seed_42_stream(category)
    for epoch in range(min(configured_epochs, 200)):
        for batch_index in range(200):
            # Preserve family-specific sampling and its internal user mapping.
            batch, internal_user_ids = inherited_training_batch_with_internal_ids(...)
            _, sequence, positive, original_negative = batch
            valid = (sequence != 0) & (positive != 0)
            eligible_counts = count_eligible_negatives(
                internal_user_ids, positive,
                exclude_padding=True,
                exclude_complete_known_training_history=True)
            supervised = valid & (eligible_counts > 0)
            N = supervised.sum()
            record_skipped_positions(valid & ~supervised)
            if N == 0:
                record_skipped_optimizer_step()
                continue
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            for example_chunk in fixed_complete_sequence_chunks(batch):
                # Full sequence context remains intact in every example.
                features = model.log2feats(example_chunk.sequence)
                positions = supervised_positions_in(example_chunk)
                negatives, negative_mask = sample_uniform_without_replacement(
                    K=32, positions=positions,
                    exclude_padding=True,
                    exclude_current_target=True,
                    exclude_complete_known_training_history=True,
                    rng=negative_rng)
                # Draw order/seed mapping is identical in CE and BCE trials.
                candidates = concatenate([positions.positive[:, None], negatives], dim=1)
                logits = existing_candidate_scores(model, features[positions], candidates)
                if objective == 'candidate_ce':
                    logits = mask_invalid_negative_logits_to_minus_infinity(logits, negative_mask)
                    losses = -logits[:, 0] + logsumexp(logits, dim=1)
                elif objective == 'group_balanced_bce':
                    losses = softplus(-logits[:, 0]) + masked_mean(
                        softplus(logits[:, 1:]), negative_mask, dim=1)
                # Immediate backward releases this example chunk's graph.
                (losses.sum() / N).backward()
            record_unclipped_gradient_norm()
            inherited_gradient_clipping_if_present()
            optimizer.step()  # Exactly once per logical batch.
        inherited_validation_and_checkpoint_selection()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint(category, model, inherited_config, training_metadata)
write_baseline_consistent_predictor_with_four_category_routing()
# Predictor gathers max(index where sequence[index] != 0).
# Preserve baseline empty-history handling; load one checkpoint/category.
# Preserve DiagnosisProbe, ModelView and B x L diagnostic loader interfaces.
# Host selects by four-category sampled-candidate macro validation HR@10.
# If available, report paired user-hit differences and descriptive bootstrap intervals.
# Record all search attempts; never infer full-catalog gains from sampled validation.

originality.positive: Provides a focused, diagnosis-driven comparison of candidate competition within the required NextItNet family, with explicit sampling, reduction and memory controls.
originality.negative: Multi-negative cross-entropy is established, including sampled-softmax precedent in NextItNet. Uncorrected candidate CE and the proposed controls constitute an experimental refinement rather than a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Establishes a useful objective control before attributing improvements to contextual gates or negative-mining curricula, and can clarify whether competitive candidate discrimination warrants further work.
future_potential.negative: Training separation may improve without validation or full-catalog gains. The mechanism only indirectly targets older-interest displacement and cannot resolve unavailable compatibility or unmet-need evidence; these limits warrant reducing the earlier score of 7.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes training candidate construction and loss while retaining the architecture, checkpoint format and inference interfaces; direct example chunking avoids additional caching machinery.
code_difficulty.negative: Distinct per-user sampling, complete-history exclusion, internal user mapping, bounded-memory backward, reproducible matched candidates and exact loss reduction require more care than the earlier score of 3 suggested.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes the residual causal dilated-convolution backbone retained in this proposal.
Provides sampled-softmax precedent for a family-preserving objective experiment.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed candidate count or objective improves this pinned four-category benchmark.
Sampled-softmax precedent does not make uncorrected candidate CE equivalent to corrected sampled softmax.

related_work.title: Wu et al., TOIS 2024: sampled-softmax analysis
contributions: The supplied search summary describes implicit hard-negative weighting and ranking benefits of sampled softmax.
Motivates comparing candidate competition while retaining baseline unnormalized logits.
limitations: Does not identify the actual bottleneck in the supplied Electronics model.
Its findings do not guarantee transfer to this NextItNet configuration.
The supplied citation is descriptive; no independently verified bibliographic details or empirical replication are claimed.

related_work.title: Hard-negative sampling theory
contributions: Supports treating negative hardness as a controllable experimental choice.
limitations: Does not establish a moderate-hard curriculum as superior for this task.
Mining changes the training distribution and requires a separate controlled experiment.

related_work.title: UFNRec
contributions: Documents false-negative risks relevant to competitive negative sampling.
limitations: Excluding known training positives does not eliminate latent false negatives.
Its teacher-based remedy is not adopted under the single-model experiment constraint.

related_work.title: PyTorch autograd backward documentation
contributions: Documents gradient accumulation across backward calls.
Supports immediate backward on independent example chunks with full-batch normalization and one optimizer update.
limitations: Accumulating graph-connected losses or using retain_graph preserves saved activations.
Chunking requires additional attention to stochastic operations, shared graphs and batch-dependent state.

related_work.title: PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss documentation
contributions: Defines the shared softmax denominator and loss reductions used to specify candidate CE.
limitations: Independent candidate-chunk cross-entropies do not reproduce one global candidate cross-entropy.
The API formula does not establish recommendation performance.

related_work.title: PyTorch BCEWithLogitsLoss documentation
contributions: Defines independent sigmoid losses and reduction behavior.
Clarifies why positive-plus-mean-negative BCE differs from a default mean over all candidate terms.
limitations: Matching candidate counts does not match CE weighting or gradient scale.
Loss reduction choices require explicit experimental specification.

related_work.title: GradCache implementation
contributions: Provides a representation-gradient caching and recomputation pattern for bounding backbone activation memory.
limitations: Exact replay requires preserving dropout RNG, parameters and model state between passes.
Tied embedding gradients and loss-side memory must also be handled; direct example chunking is preferred here.

related_work.title: Cut Cross-Entropy
contributions: Provides implementations that avoid materializing the complete logits matrix.
Documents an exact configuration useful for checking numerical equivalence without gradient filtering.
limitations: It is not required for the proposed 33-candidate objective and is not assumed to be installed.
Manual candidate-axis streaming requires a shared global denominator and correctly scaled recomputed gradients.

related_work.title: TensorFlow sampled-softmax loss documentation
contributions: Documents expected-count corrections and accidental-hit handling in corrected sampled softmax.
limitations: Corrections must match the actual sampling and exclusion policy.
The proposed uncorrected candidate CE does not implement this estimator.

related_work.title: TensorFlow candidate-sampling reference
contributions: Explains candidate-sampling objectives and expected-count corrections.
limitations: Positive inclusion and negative inclusion can differ, so uniform negative sampling does not imply all corrections cancel.
Finite-sample approximations do not automatically recover full-catalog likelihood.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics, including model orderings.
limitations: Does not invalidate the pinned benchmark as the required selection objective.
Fixed candidates improve comparability but do not establish full-catalog generalization.

related_work.title: SciPy bootstrap documentation
contributions: Defines paired resampling, supporting aligned user-level comparisons.
Provides methodological grounding for category-stratified paired bootstrap analysis.
limitations: The proposed stratified macro analysis must preserve category weights and any user dependence.
Conditional intervals exclude training and candidate-redraw variation and do not correct validation selection.

related_work.title: Cawley and Talbot: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains overfitting of model-selection criteria and resulting optimistic performance estimates.
limitations: Bootstrapping only the selected winner does not evaluate the complete selection procedure.
Confirmatory evaluation requires independent assessment; this task delegates final held-out evaluation to the host.
